name: Cersei
summary: An unusually complete Rust SDK for building coding agents, documented like infrastructure and benchmarked against the frameworks it means to displace.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: A Rust SDK with per-capability crates plus built-in MCP integration and a bundled CLI, so an agent can be built with it and an existing agent can reach its tools over MCP. Documentation is fully public and machine-readable (a 'Copy Markdown' affordance is offered on pages).

hlido_opinion.headline: An unusually complete Rust SDK for building coding agents, documented like infrastructure and benchmarked against the frameworks it means to displace.
hlido_opinion.body: Cersei is the agent SDK for people who were going to write one anyway. It ships the pieces a production coding agent actually needs — tool execution, LLM streaming, sub-agent orchestration, persistent memory backed by an embedded graph database, skills, MCP integration — as composable library functions rather than a framework you submit to, and it is modular by crate (cersei-types, cersei-provider, cersei-tools, cersei-agent, cersei-memory, cersei-hooks, cersei-mcp) with a facade that re-exports everything. The documentation is the strongest signal on the surface: alongside the expected quick start and API reference there are cookbooks for custom tools, deployment, embedding in apps, research and graph-memory agents, an architecture section with a crate map and data flow, a comparisons page against Agno, LangGraph, CrewAI and PydanticAI, and separate benchmark pages for the library, graph memory, the bundled CLI, and a head-to-head against Claude Code and Codex, including LongMemEval for memory. Publishing a 'when we lose' comparison and naming the specific benchmark suites is the behaviour of a project that expects to be measured. AgentRL is the ambitious part and the part to treat carefully: agents that trace their own failures, propose fixes in isolated sandboxes, promote whichever passes verification and register it as a reusable tool, so they get cheaper on recurring problems. That is a strong claim about self-improvement and the public surface asserts it without showing a longitudinal result. Two practical caveats: it is Rust, which is a real adoption gate in a Python-dominated space, and the public surface offers documentation but no access or pricing statement and no conversion path beyond reading, so the required call-to-action check fails. For a Rust team building an agent product, this is one of the few serious options. For a Python team, the comparison page is useful and the SDK is not.

tier_rationale: STEADY (70) because the documented surface is deep and self-critical — crate map, data flow, named-competitor comparison and four separate benchmark pages — which is far more than this category typically publishes. It is held below VITAL because the headline AgentRL self-improvement claim is asserted rather than demonstrated with published longitudinal evidence, because every benchmark is vendor-run, and because the surface has no access, support or call-to-action statement at all.
what_it_does_well: Ships as composable library functions and separable crates rather than an all-or-nothing framework
Documentation covers architecture, crate map and data flow — not just a quick start
Publishes a direct comparison page against Agno, LangGraph, CrewAI and PydanticAI
Names its benchmark suites, including LongMemEval for memory and a head-to-head against Claude Code and Codex
Persistent memory with an embedded graph database is a first-class component, not an add-on
MCP integration is built in, which makes it addressable by the wider agent tooling ecosystem
Cookbooks cover realistic shapes of work (custom tools, deployment, embedding, research agents)
what_it_fails_at: AgentRL's self-improvement claim is the headline and has no published longitudinal evidence behind it
All benchmarks are vendor-run; no third-party reproduction is linked
Rust-only, which excludes most of the agent-building population regardless of technical merit
No call-to-action, access statement, pricing or support terms anywhere on the surface
Project identity is diffuse — Cersei, the Atlas project and an 'Abstract CLI' appear as one surface with unclear boundaries
The breadth (sandboxes, VMs, embeddings, compression, AST intelligence) raises a maintenance question the surface does not answer
best_for: Rust teams building a coding agent or embedding one in an existing service
Builders who want to assemble an agent from parts rather than adopt a framework's control flow
Agents that need persistent, queryable memory rather than a vector blob
Teams that need the agent in-process for latency or deployment reasons
not_recommended_for: Python-first teams — the comparison page is the only useful part for you
Anyone needing a supported product with documented terms rather than an open SDK
Buyers who require independent verification before trusting memory or latency benchmarks
Teams wanting a hosted agent runtime instead of a library
red_flags: AgentRL is described as producing agents that diagnose their own failures and promote verified fixes into reusable tools. This is a significant claim about autonomous self-improvement and the public surface offers no measured result over time to support it — treat it as a research direction, not a shipped guarantee.
Every benchmark on the surface, including the comparisons against named competitors and against Claude Code and Codex, is run by the project itself.

compared_to.verdict_diff: Agno is a Python agent framework with a large install base; Cersei is Rust and library-shaped. Cersei's own comparison page addresses Agno directly — read it, then pick on language before features.

LangChain is the ecosystem default with the widest integration surface and the heaviest abstractions. Cersei is narrower, faster and far less adopted. LangChain for breadth and hiring, Cersei for in-process Rust control.
PydanticAI is the typed, minimal Python option and the closest in philosophy. If you like Cersei's composable approach but need Python, that is where to look.

evidence_urls.claim: Rust SDK shipping tool execution, LLM streaming, sub-agent orchestration, graph memory, skills and MCP as composable crates
Public comparison page against Agno, LangGraph, CrewAI and PydanticAI
Named benchmark pages including LongMemEval and a head-to-head against Claude Code and Codex
AgentRL self-improving-agent capability described on the docs surface
